data.title: REG - Tata Steel Limited - Disclosure under 30 & 51 SEBI Listing Regulations
data.description:
RNS Number : 4540V Tata Steel Limited 18 September 2026  

Ref: SEC/1069/2026-27

September 18, 2026

London Stock Exchange

London

Dear Madam, Sirs,

Sub: Disclosure under Regulations 30 read with 51 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015

This is further to our disclosures dated April 2, 2024 and May 24, 2024 on the abovementioned subject read with 'material litigation' section of the Board's Report of Tata Steel Limited ('Company') and notes to financial statements, both forming part of the 11th Integrated Report and 118th Annual Accounts of the Company for FY2025-26, in connection with loans obligations of the Company arising from Steel Development Fund ('SDF').

Background:

On April 2, 2024, the Company filed a writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta ('Hon'ble High Court'), in the matter of rejection of a representation made by the Company in respect of waiver of loans availed by the Company from SDF (in parity with SAIL), managed by Joint Plant Committee ('JPC'), Ministry of Steel. The matter was heard by the Hon'ble High Court over several hearings.

On May 24, 2024, the Hon'ble High Court (Single Bench) dismissed the writ petition filed by the Company, with a liberty to the Company to approach the JPC. The Company sought further legal remedies and filed an appeal against this order before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta (Division Bench). This appeal is pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta.

On January 17, 2025, the Company received a demand from the Ministry of Steel to make payment towards outstanding balance of SDF loan. During FY2026, the Company discharged its liability towards JPC aggregating to ₹2,970 crore, without prejudice to its rights and contentions in the appeal.

Present Status:

The Management believed that an interim protection was necessary to safeguard the amounts deposited by the Company with JPC. Accordingly, the Company filed an Interim Application bearing IA no. GA/2/2026 before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta seeking injunction on JPC utilizing the said amount of ₹2,970 crore.

The IA NO. GA/2/2026 was heard by the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta on September 17, 2026.

As per the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta dated September 17, 2026 received by the Company today i.e. September 18, 2026, Hon'ble High Court has disposed of the interim application with the direction that till the appeal is disposed of, the fund shall not be utilised or disbursed to third parties.

This disclosure is being made by the Company in compliance with Regulations 30 and 51 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended.

This is for your information and records.

data.title: Two-Year U.S. Treasury Yield Reaches New Multi-Year High
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani

The two-year U.S. Treasury yield rose as markets grew more confident the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates to fight inflation.

The two-year yield touched 4.744% on Friday, its highest intraday yield since July 2024 when it hit 4.775%.

The Fed raised rates Wednesday and Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks left markets under the impression that more increases could come.

Since then, the yield curve has been flattening. The spread between the two-year and the 10-year yields reached its narrowest level since March 2025 on Thursday, before widening slightly on Friday.

The 10-year yield was recently at 4.998%.

According to the CME's FedWatch tool, futures markets price in a 58% chance of a rate boost in October, up from 55% on Thursday.

Write to Paulo Trevisani at paulo.trevisani@wsj.com

data.title: Disney Beefs Up Tech Ambitions With Newly Created CTO Role — WSJ
data.description:
By Ben Fritz

Disney has hired the head of artificial intelligence company Character.AI to be its first ever chief technology officer, as chief executive Josh D'Amaro tries to improve the entertainment giant's digital prowess.

Karandeep Anand will oversee Disney's internal technology and infrastructure, data and AI platforms, and product and engineering teams, reporting directly to D'Amaro, the company said Friday.

Disney said "a number of" Anand's technical team from Character.AI will also join the entertainment company. Before leading Character.AI, Anand held executive roles at Meta and Microsoft. He was appointed CEO of Character.AI in June 2025.

The startup allows users to interact with AI-powered chatbot avatars ranging from real people like Elon Musk to anime characters and a generic therapist.

Earlier this year, Character.AI and Google, which licensed the startup's technology in an earlier deal, settled lawsuits with the families of teenagers who killed or harmed themselves after interacting with Character.AI's chatbot. The incidents were before Anand's tenure.

Disney said Anand led Character.AI through a period of rapid growth "while also making user trust and safety a priority as the platform scaled."

D'Amaro, who became CEO in March, has said Disney needs to move faster to directly connect with fans online, rather than just relying on its traditional strength in theme parks and on movie screens. One of his top priorities is making Disney+ a consumer touchpoint for all of the company's businesses, not just television.

A challenge reaching that goal has been that different business units have long run their technology with significant degrees of independence. The company has also announced technology initiatives that fizzled, like an integration with OpenAI's scrapped video app Sora, or have yet to bear fruit, like a virtual world in development with "Fortnite" maker Epic Games.

Disney said Anand will modernize how it builds and delivers technology company-wide.

On Thursday, Disney promoted former Google and YouTube executive Adam Smith to chairman of its streaming business, putting another Silicon Valley veteran in a senior position.

Write to Ben Fritz at ben.fritz@wsj.com

data.title: Virginia tightens data center restrictions amid political backlash
data.description:
The US state of Virginia is tightening permitting, commercial and environmental controls on data centers as political backlash grows against the server warehouses and the technology developed within them, Governor Abigail Spanberger said on Friday.

Virginia, which has the largest concentration of data centers in the world, unveiled plans that include banning non-disclosure agreements and imposing clean energy mandates on the projects.

The move follows a spate of recent similar steps taken by governors in New York, Texas and Pennsylvania to crack down on the rapid expansion of data centers, which are increasingly being developed to train and roll out artificial intelligence.

Virginia's "Data Center Accountability Framework" is aimed at easing the public's concerns around data center development secrecy and the impact that the energy-intensive facilities have on power bills and the environment, Spanberger told a press conference.

"Community members are demanding action," Spanberger said.

The ban on non-disclosure agreements would apply to projects for data centers of 25 megawatts or more. Data centers will also be offered incentives to develop renewable solar and wind power backup generators, instead of natural gas or diesel-fired ones, to help power their operations, the governor said.

Part of the framework will be subject to approval by state legislators next year.

data.title: These fast-growing ETFs aim for yields as high as 17.5%. But here's the catch.
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

So-called autocallable ETFs pay coupons like bonds but are linked to equity risk

Autocallables are a complex corner of Wall Street - and they're now gaining traction in the exchange-traded-fund industry.

A niche corner of the derivatives world is colliding with the universe of excahnge-traded funds.

So-called autocallable ETFs have emerged as a fast-growing area within the booming ETF industry, where investors are increasingly gravitating toward more complicated, actively managed products, some of which feature derivatives like options and swaps.

The growing popularity of these products hinges on a tantalizing hook: bond-like yield payments that may, in some cases, exceed 15% as a target. But they are also subject to equity-style risks that could result in losses for investors.

Autocallable ETFs listed in the U.S. held $4.8 billion in assets as of Sept. 10, up from just $580 million at the end of 2025, according to Aniket Ullal, head of ETF research and analytics at CFRA Research. Fund launches in the space have also picked up; so far, 25 new autocallable ETFs have made their debut in 2026 through Sept. 10, compared with six in all of 2025.

To be sure, the space is still a rounding error compared with the trillions of dollars in U.S.-listed ETFs overall. But the growth rate has caught the attention of some investment professionals who worry the attractive yields are causing some to overlook, or otherwise miss, the risks.

"It's going crazy," said Ken Nuttall, CIO at BlackDiamond Wealth Management. Some funds are "getting sold mainly on yield," he noted, "and people don't understand the risk that they're taking for it."

How it works

Autocallable notes are structured-debt instruments tied to stocks or an index with underlying equity exposure. Investor payouts, and the return of principal, ultimately hinges on how the underlying reference asset trades compared with predetermined levels. ETFs in this category typically replicate an autocallable-like payoff using swaps, rather than holding the notes directly.

Lofty yields are the draw: Funds in this space commonly estimate an annualized rate in the 10% to 15% range, according to Zachary Evens, a manager research analyst at Morningstar. That is well above what bonds typically pay. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note BX:TMUBMUSD10Y rose to 5% as recently as Wednesday to settle at its highest level since 2007. The yield on junk bonds in the U.S. was recently around 7.5%.

But there's a catch: a barrier level that, once triggered, starts a clock. Typically, investors immediately stop receiving their coupon payments, and if the reference asset hasn't recovered past the barrier by the time the underlying contract matures, investors will risk losing principal.

Just how much of that principal is lost depends in part on the magnitude of the selloff in equities tied to the underlying reference index. If a barrier is breached with, say, a 30% drop in the reference index, that large loss would hit the autocallables in the portfolio, provided the underlying assets failed to recover by the time the notes matured. The loss to principal would be offset by any monthly coupons received prior to maturity, but there are some twists to consider. Distributions could resume if the reference index moves back above the barrier, and investors could also get all their capital back at the maturity of the autocallable contracts if the index's decline is less than the one set by the crucial barrier level.

Another important feature of such ETFs is they may invest in many autocallables, so investor capital may be spread across multiple contracts with different maturities. That could help mitigate potential losses.

The largest such ETF is the FT Vest Laddered Autocallable Barrier & Income ETF ACYN, which has around $2 billion in assets. The ETF's underlying stock-market exposures may be tied to more than one index, such as the S&P 500 SPX, the Russell 2000 RUT and the Nasdaq-100 NDX, and its returns are linked to the worst performer among them. That means losses may occur if the worst-performing underlying equity index is below the maturity barrier when autocallables in its portfolio expire.

The ETF takes a laddered approach to investing in autocallables, resulting in staggered maturities. That is just one example; the strategy has varying structures and rules that set the path of potential outcomes.

 
5 biggest autocallable ETFs                                    Assets 
FT Vest Laddered Autocallable Barrier & Income ETF             $1,963,960,947 
Calamos Autocallable Income ETF                                $1,314,191,754 
FT Vest Laddered Autocallable Barrier & Resilient Income ETF   $437,820,408 
Calamos Nasdaq Autocallable Income ETF                         $349,434,064 
Calamos Autocallable Growth ETF                                $150,925,602 
Source: Morningstar data on 9/11/2026

While many autocallable ETFs have coupon barriers, funds launched by ProShares in August do not, Simeon Hyman, global investment strategist at ProShares, told MarketWatch in an interview. Such is the case for the ProShares S&P 500 Autocallable Income ETF ACSP, which recently had an estimated annualized yield around 19%, he said. The general trade-off in autocallables is that the "powerful" stream of income investors may receive comes with the risk of losing money if the underlying assets are down by a "material amount" at the maturity of the contracts, Hyman noted.

While many autocallable ETFs are linked to indexes with underlying equity exposures, some are linked to single stocks - like the GraniteShares Autocallable NVDA ETF ANV, which seeks to provide monthly income by investing in a portfolio of autocallables tied to shares of Nvidia (NVDA). The ETF had an annualized distribution rate of around 14% as recently as Sept. 16, according to data on GraniteShares's website.

"It's so important for investors and advisers to do their homework, because there are so many different flavors of these even in this very young space," Evens said.

The Calamos Autocallable Income ETF CAIE, the second-largest ETF in the category, helped pave the way to the strategy's uptake in the exchange-traded-fund industry. It was the first such ETF launched, in June 2025, and now has around $1.3 billion in assets.

The fund provides underlying exposure to the MerQube US Large-Cap Vol Advantage Index, which uses futures to target 35% implied volatility on the S&P 500, in order to sustain its distributions - currently calculated at a roughly 14% weighted average coupon, according to Matt Kaufman, head of ETFs at Calamos Investments.

A steep decline in the MerQube index that exceeds 40% would breach both the coupon and maturity barriers, putting investor capital at risk of losses. Because the ETF is targeting volatility that's above current levels for the S&P 500, the benchmark for U.S. large-cap stocks needn't fall quite as far as the MerQube index to hit the barrier, according to Kaufman. On the flip side, a change in the current stock-market environment resulting in a huge spike in volatility exceeding 35% would mean the S&P 500 could see a huge drop of more than 40% before the reference MerQube index breached its barrier level.

Calamos uses a strategy called laddering to try and manage this downside risk. The fund holds more than 50 autocallables with staggered five-year maturities. As they don't all mature at the same time, the losses wouldn't come all at once in an ugly bear market, with the laddering leaving some room for the market to bounce back above the critical maturity barrier for each autocallable contract.

What to watch

The autocallables notes are synthetic, in that their returns are generated through swap agreements.

Besides downside risks associated with autocallables, investors should also know that when the reference assets rise to a certain level ahead of their maturity, then they may be called away. An ETF might then reinvest the returned capital into a new autocallable contract, with new terms that could include a smaller coupon.

The big risk for investors in autocallables, though, is a major drawdown in the reference assets that fails to recover back above the maturity barrier in a severe and prolonged bear market. The longer a financial crisis or bear market stretches on, more autocallables held by the ETF may be at risk of losses should they expire with their maturity barriers still breached.

But that hasn't stopped a big-name manager from recently entering this corner of the market.

Recently, Cathie Wood - who rose to fame during the pandemic on the popularity of her firm ARK Investment Management's ETFs, which have disruptive innovation as a thematic investment theme -has now launched an autocallable ETF as its first income strategy. ARK announced in August that the ETF was targeting a 17.5% coupon.

That's the firm's estimate of a potential annualized rate for the ARK Active Autocallable Income ETF ARKY, whose portfolio of autocallable notes are linked to individual stocks the firm sees benefiting from disruptive innovation, ARK's president and COO, Tom Staudt, said in an interview.

"Our part of the universe" is well suited for autocallable notes because the reference stocks "naturally have higher volatility," he said. "Effectively, what this fund is doing is monetizing that volatility and turning it into an income stream."

Looking inside the ETF's autocallable portfolio, the maturity and coupon barriers may be breached when the reference stocks plunge by around 50% to 55%, according to Staudt. The ETF is exposed to about 50 reference stocks, each with multiple autocallable contacts, he said - adding that terms of the notes vary, with different maturities, barriers, coupons and points at which they may be called away. But with this particular ETF, missed coupons may be recouped should the reference asset climb back above the barrier, Staudt noted.

data.title: Take project delays seriously: Rajnath Singh cautions HAL over Tejas LCA delivery lags
data.description:
With Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) missing key deadlines to deliver the Tejas LCA Mk-1A, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday publicly expressed concern over “project delays” and directed the state-owned aerospace firm to take the issue “seriously”, cautioning that continued lags lead to “cost escalations” and impacts the IAF’s military capabilities.

Singh’s strong-worded speech was delivered during a ceremony the HAL organised at it own airport in the heart of the city to hand over two LCA FOC trainers, same numbers of HTT-40 basic trainers to the IAF and four Dhruv Next Generation (NG) civilian helicopters to Pawan Hans Ltd to operate for the ONGC.

“There are some issues on which we have to work. Among them is the most important issue of delays. We face delays because of technical issues, projects. We need to take these delays seriously. Because these delays create military capability gaps and the force’s requirements are not met. These delays also lead to cost escalations,” the Defence Minister stressed in the presence of the top brass and other employees of the HAL, indicating at the repeated failure of the induction of the LCA Mk-1A into the IAF.

Time Realisation

He also stated that by the time technology realisation takes place, it becomes “obsolete” due to availability of of better version globally. The government has already given a go ahead to the prototype development of the fifth generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), which is indigenously designed and developed by the DRDO.

As per the contract for 83 LCA Mk-1A signed in 2021 at a value of close to ₹46,000 crore, the HAL was supposed to have started the deliveries of the indigenous fighter aircraft from March 2024 and complete it by September 2033. But, it missed a few deadlines. The initial delay was owing to supply of F404 engines by US-based GE Aerospace which attributed it to global supply chain disruptions, forced due to the covid pandemic.

HAL CMD Ravi K in an interview to businessline the previous day clarified that the delays are due to certain software integration issues but assured that others parameters including trials for firing of weapons have been completed.

Delays

He also stated that the HAL will hand over ten fighter aircrafts to the IAF by March, 2026, since they have received ten F404 engines so far from the GE Aerospace. According to him, the GE has promised 12 additional engines by December, this year.

Rajnath Singh public outburst follows repeated criticism by Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh over delay of LCA Mk-1A handing over. On February 10, 2025, during a conversation with HAL officials at Aero India 2025 in Bengaluru, the IAF Chief had said, “I was promised that when I come here in February, we will have 11 Mk-1As ready minus the engine. And not a single one is ready yet....”

“HAL is our own company, we all have worked there... everything is ho jaayega [it will happen],” he had remarked that went viral at that point of time. Incidentally, Air Chief Marshal Singh was also present at the function.

Futuristic Ideas

During his speech, the Defence Minister also posed a challenge to come up with futuristic technologies which does not exist. “Today, I want to give one challenge to our young scientists, engineers, designers, test pilots and technicians to create technologies that do not exist today. You have to develop such capabilities which will provide India a leading position in the global aerospace technology landscape in the decades to come,” he said towards the end of his address.

Earlier in his speech, he described the handing over of platforms as a significant milestone in the nation’s progress towards indigenous aerospace capability, technological self-confidence and self-reliance. “Our aim is to make India capable, self-reliant, and globally competitive in meeting its aerospace requirements,” he said.

Speaking on the occasion, Minister of Civil Aviation K Rammohan Naidu said that the certification and induction of the Dhruv NG into civil operations marked an important milestone for India’s indigenous civil aviation ecosystem. He termed it as a reflection of the growing capability of Indian industry to develop and support advanced aerospace platforms for commercial applications.

The CMD HAL Ravi K stated that handing over of Tejas FOC Twin Seater Trainers, HTT 40 Basic Trainers and Dhruv NG helicopters demonstrates HAL’s ability to develop and deliver platforms for diverse civil and defence requirements.

data.title: Anil Ambani denies 'any wrongdoing' after CBI lodges FIR over ₹2,684-cr LIC investment 'fraud'
data.description:
Reliance Group chairman Anil Ambani on Friday denied any wrongdoing after the CBI registered a case against Reliance Capital Limited (RCAP), its former chairman, former group managing director Satish Seth, unidentified public servants and others in connection with an alleged ₹2,684.57-crore fraud involving investments made by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).

A spokesperson for Ambani, in a statement, said, "The FIR registered by the CBI pertains to Reliance Capital Limited. Ambani served as a Non-Executive Director/Chairman of the Board of Reliance Capital Limited from 2005 until November 2021, when the Reserve Bank of India superseded the Board of Directors of the company and appointed an Administrator." "Ambani denies any wrongdoing, whatsoever, and reserves all rights available to him in law," the spokesperson added.

The FIR was registered on the basis of a written complaint received from the LIC against RCAP, Ambani, Seth, unidentified public servants and others, an official statement said.

According to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the LIC has alleged that between April 12, 2012, and March 9, 2018, it subscribed to five non-convertible debentures (NCDs) issued by RCAP, aggregating to ₹3,900 crore.

The investments were made for "general corporate purposes, funding requirements and refinancing of existing debt", the statement said.

The LIC has alleged that the accused persons "entered a criminal conspiracy" and committed offences, including "cheating, criminal breach of trust, criminal misconduct, diversion/misappropriation of funds and falsification of accounts".

The CBI said the LIC has alleged that the accused persons dishonestly induced it to invest in RCAP through "misrepresentation" and thereafter, "fraudulently diverted the said funds".

The alleged acts caused a "wrongful loss to the tune of ₹2,684.57 crore to LIC" and corresponding wrongful gain to the accused and other beneficiaries, the statement said.

Investigation has been taken up to identify the role of all those involved, including public servants and private individuals, examine the alleged criminal conspiracy and trace the end-use or diversion of the invested funds, it said.

The CBI said it had earlier registered eight FIRs against Reliance Communications Limited, Reliance Capital Limited, Reliance Home Finance Limited, Reliance Commercial Finance Limited and Reliance Telecom Limited on complaints received from various public-sector banks, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and the LIC.

The agency said it has so far filed six chargesheets and arrested seven accused persons in these cases.

The cases are under investigation and are being monitored by the Supreme Court, it said.

data.title: Who is Howard Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman?
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway said Howard Buffett would become the chairman of the $1.1 trillion conglomerate, succeeding legendary investor Warren Buffett, who would become chairman emeritus.

The move completes one of the biggest and most closely watched transitions in corporate America, nine months after the Oracle ‌of Omaha handed the CEO reins to longtime lieutenant Greg Abel.

Here are some key facts about Howard Buffett:

WARREN BUFFETT'S OLDEST SON

Warren, 96, has three children: Susie, Howard and Peter. Howard, 71, is the second-born and the eldest of his two sons.

LONG-TIME BERKSHIRE DIRECTOR

Known as Howie, he has been a Berkshire director for 33 years, a longer apprenticeship than what Warren served before taking the reins.

LONG-STANDING SUCCESSOR

Howard's appointment as the non-executive chairman of Berkshire is part of the conglomerate's long-standing succession plan.

In 2011, Warren told CBS News that he would like Howard to succeed him.

PRESERVING BERKSHIRE'S CULTURE

In his new role, Howard's responsibility would be to preserve Berkshire's culture. He would not have a management ​role as chairman.

Howard had his own definition of Berkshire's culture.

"It's not rocket science," he had told ​the Wall Street Journal in January 2025. "The culture is to keep things simple, to do what you need to do but don't do a lot of things you don't need to do, treat people fairly, ​respect your managers, respect your shareholders. Tell them the bad news upfront, be honest."

DONNED MULTIPLE HATS

Over the course of his life, Howard has been a farmer, photographer, conservationist and businessman.

He has previously served on the Douglas County Board of Commissioners in Nebraska, two Office of the United States Trade Representative committees, and non-profit organization Commission on Presidential Debates.

He also worked in law enforcement for about a decade, including as sheriff of Macon County, Illinois.

Howard has authored more than a dozen books on conservation, wildlife and the human condition, including two New York Times bestsellers. He was also the executive producer of award-winning documentary films.

MEMBER OF SEVERAL CORPORATE BOARDS

Howard has served as director of several corporate boards, including Agro Tech, Archer-Daniels Midland, Conagra Foods, the Coca-Cola Company, Coca Cola Enterprises, FirsTier Financial, and Lindsay Corporation.

ADDRESSING GLOBAL HUNGER

Howard leads the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, a private charitable foundation that works to address global hunger, combat human trafficking and mitigate conflicts.

Established in 1999, the foundation has been funded by donations from Warren Buffett and has devoted resources in recent years to Ukraine during its war with Russia.

AROUND THE WORLD

Howard has traveled to more than 150 countries around the world, in part due to his charitable work.

MULTIPLE HONORS

Howard has been honored by several governments, including Colombia, El Salvador, Mexico, Rwanda and Ukraine for his charitable work.

He has also been recognized for his contributions in agriculture, conservation, journalism, philanthropy and law enforcement.

data.title: Nvidia Chip Sales Could Double Next Year, CEO Jensen Huang Says — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark

Nvidia is already the dominant artificial-intelligence chip company. But its reach could extend even further next year, if CEO Jensen Huang is to be believed.

Speaking while on a trip to the U.K. on Thursday, Huang made a striking forecast-that he expects Nvidia to sell "twice as many chips next year as we do this year."

That was surprising. First, Nvidia doesn't generally give out forecasts about individual chip shipments. Second, it's a big number for a company that is already doing hundreds of billions in annual sales and has said it is constrained by supply-chain issues.

Huang was talking about chip volumes rather than overall revenue. Nvidia is already forecast to achieve 70% sales growth for its next fiscal year, which will end in January 2028, making it largely the same as the calendar year.

So chip volumes could double, but sales are expected to rise around 70%. Nvidia didn't respond to a Barron's request for comment to clarify what chips are included in the "twice as many" forecast, but Huang did say the driver was AI. That suggests the engine of growth will be the company's AI-related graphics-processing units (GPUs), central-processing units (CPUs) and networking chips rather than its video-gaming hardware.

While Nvidia doesn't disclose individual chip numbers, analysis firm Epoch AI estimates it sold around 4.46 million AI GPUs in 2025 and had sold about 3.39 million this year through the end of August. Assuming its monthly rate of sales stayed the same-a big assumption as Nvidia is ramping up production of its next-generation Vera Rubin hardware-that would put it on track to sell about 5.09 million AI GPUs this year.

That's not a rate of growth that would imply doubling volumes next year, but there are a few things to consider. Increasingly, Nvidia sells its AI chips via its NV72 server racks, which package together 72 GPUs as well as 36 CPUs and a number of networking chips. Huang might be including the total number of chips across the server rack in his estimate.

The numbers add up quickly when you count all the chips within a server and assume racks will account for a greater share of future sales.

Max Weinbach, an analyst at market-research firm Creative Strategies, estimated earlier this year that Nvidia was set to ship between 70,000 and 80,000 of its Grace Blackwell server racks this year. Assuming all of them were NV72 configurations, the midpoint would indicate 5.4 million AI GPUs, 2.7 million CPUs, and millions of networking chips.

So what about 2027? Research firm TrendForce estimates that shipments of NVL72 racks will grow by more than 50% in 2027 from this year. That could account for a substantial part of Huang's doubling forecast and imply huge revenue growth, since Vera Rubin hardware will come at higher average prices than Blackwell racks.

However, volume growth outstripping revenue growth indicates Nvidia also expects to sell a lot of lower-priced chips. One candidate is stand-alone CPUs, which the company launched this year and said it expects to become a multibillion-dollar business.

Other possible products to account for the remaining volumes include AI chips for the Chinese market, stand-alone networking chips, and the company's new PC chip, which it unveiled earlier this year.

Nvidia might not like talking too much about individual chip sales anymore, but it's still worth shareholders having an idea of how the world's largest company intends to keep growing.

Nvidia shares were down 0.2% in early trading Friday.

Write to Adam Clark at adam.clark@barrons.com

data.title: US factory production falls in August; outlook clouded by rising costs
data.description:
Key points:
  • Manufacturing production falls 0.3% in August after rising for seven straight months
  • Utilities production jumps 1.8%; mining output edges up 0.1%
  • Overall industrial production unchanged; rises 1.4% on year-over-year basis

By Lucia Mutikani

US factory production unexpectedly fell in August and higher oil prices and rising interest rates could offset some of the support from an artificial intelligence buildout, likely keeping activity moderate for the rest of the year.

The decline in output, reported by the Federal Reserve on Friday, followed seven straight months of increases. The US central bank on Wednesday raised interest rates for the first time in three years and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead. Oil prices are hovering above $100 a barrel with no end in sight to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

"Looking ahead, we think manufacturing output will rise a little further over coming months, but will fail to match the pace set in the first half of this year," said Samuel Tombs, chief US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. "Some manufacturers likely will find that demand softens as they pass on higher energy prices to consumers."

Manufacturing output dropped 0.3% last month following an unrevised 0.2% rise in July. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast production would increase 0.3%. Output advanced 0.9% on a year-over-year basis in August, a modest increase that, according to some economists, indicated the Trump administration's aggressive trade policy had not had the desired effect of rejuvenating the nation's industrial base.

Production in the sector, which accounts for about 9.4% of the economy, received a boost in prior months as businesses rushed orders to avoid shortages and higher prices from the escalation of the war in the Middle East.

The decline in August was led by a 0.5% drop in the production of long-lasting manufactured goods.

Motor vehicles and parts production decreased 1.2%, notching a second straight monthly decline. Output of computers and peripheral equipment fell 1.4%, but was up 5.5% on a year-over-year basis. Production of communications equipment increased 0.8%. Though the output of semiconductors and related electronic components dipped 0.1%, this category was up 12.4% from a year ago.

The AI spending spree has cushioned the blow from import tariffs on manufacturing. Some economists are still betting on a strong manufacturing performance this year, despite a sharp rise in longer-dated US Treasury yields in recent weeks and the Fed's decision to raise its benchmark overnight interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range.

POSSIBLE TAILWIND FROM HIGHER DEFENSE SPENDING

"We still look for manufacturing activity to pick up through next year, and the AI infrastructure buildout is a key reason for our sanguine outlook," said Bernard Yaros, lead U.S. economist at Oxford Economics. "The demand case for AI still seems strong enough to shrug off higher-for-longer rates and increased geopolitical risk. Greater defense spending will also act as another tailwind."

Restocking by businesses that have run down inventories for five straight quarters to meet robust demand could also provide a lift to manufacturing, though some economists argued that trend could be overshadowed by the drag from rising costs.

Production of nondurable goods was unchanged after falling 0.4% in July. Rises in output at textile mills as well as for apparel and leather products were offset by declines in the production of plastics and rubber goods, and petroleum and coal.

"Factory output shows the first signs of a slowdown which could worsen if the geopolitical headwinds intensify and diesel fuel prices do not come back down," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS.

"Soaring energy prices are costly for industry and higher diesel prices may start to chip away at the manufacturing renaissance picture painted by White House economic officials."

Mining production edged up 0.1% last month, matching the rise in July. Oil and gas well drilling increased 0.9% after accelerating by 5.2% in July. Utilities production shot up 1.8% after climbing 0.5% in July.

Overall industrial production was unchanged last month after gaining 0.2% in July. Industrial output advanced 1.4% on a year-over-year basis in August. Capacity utilization for the industrial sector, a measure of how fully firms are using their resources, was unchanged at 76.3% in August. It is 3.1 percentage points below its 1972–2025 average.

The operating rate for the manufacturing sector fell 0.3 percentage points to 75.7%. It is 2.5 percentage points below its long-run average.

"There is no evidence here that tariffs or anything are generating an influx of new jobs in manufacturing and industry," said Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics.

data.title: Net-a-Porter's CEO Can't Get Enough of Customers Complaining — WSJ
data.description:
By Suzanne Kapner

At a dinner last year for 25 Net-a-Porter customers at the online luxury retailer's London headquarters, Chief Executive Heather Kaminetsky asked a simple question: How can we do better?

It's something she has been asking every chance she gets since taking the helm in April 2025 with the marching orders to turn around the struggling company.

Customers have had a lot to say.

Net-a-Porter pioneered selling designer clothes and accessories online when it was founded in 2000. But it struggled after Swiss watch and jewelry conglomerate Richemont bought a majority stake in 2010. Customers complained of inconsistent service, lost packages and delayed returns. The retailer tried to appeal to a broader swath of aspirational shoppers with less expensive items and deeper discounts, further alienating its high-end clientele.

As sales shrunk and losses piled up, Richemont looked for a buyer. It sold Net-a-Porter, plus a men's site called Mr. Porter and another online retailer Yoox, to the parent of Mytheresa, which had cracked the code of selling luxury online. Richemont subsidized the purchase by loading the deal with cash and credit in exchange for roughly a third of the shares of the holding company, now called LuxExperience.

It installed Kaminetsky, Mytheresa's North American president, to lead Net-a-Porter. The bet was that it could return to profitability by restoring its fashion authority and making its clients feel like they were part of an exclusive club.

Kaminetsky had come up through luxury, known for wooing customers in marketing jobs at Barneys New York and Net-a-Porter more than a decade ago.

"There was an opportunity to win back customers who had lapsed over the course of many years," said Kaminetsky, who is 47 years old. To do that, she realized she first needed to talk to these women.

She zeroed in on Net-a-Porter's top customers. About 4% of its shoppers account for almost half its sales.

She sent thousands of emails to clients introducing herself and asking for feedback. She invited customers for fireside chats with Net-a-Porter employees. She increased the number of designer events, hosting more in the past year than Net-a-Porter did in the prior three years combined. At one with Burberry, guests could purchase and customize vintage trench coats. At another with Carolina Herrera, guests were transported by luxury train to an estate in the British countryside for dinner in a vineyard.

Other luxury retailers court their top customers with attention and exclusive access. A challenge with this strategy is that retailers need to keep upping the ante to come up with distinctive perks, and it is competitive.

At every event, Kaminetsky handed out her contact information in case shoppers wanted to follow up. She got an earful.

Customers wanted more personalized service from their personal shoppers. They wanted a greater selection of both established brands and newer labels. They wanted a more sophisticated package-tracking system and streamlined returns process. The delivery drivers should wear snappier uniforms, they said.

Some ideas were rejected as impractical, like the shopper who suggested Net-a-Porter deliver packages by private jet. But Kaminetsky has adopted many other suggestions.

Return labels now arrive in the box and all customers have to do is paste them on the package. No need for any forms or printing.

Net-a-Porter delivery drivers now wear uniforms from Mr. Porter. Before they could wear any dark-colored clothing.

Kaminetsky expanded same-day delivery to more locations, including the Jersey Shore, after shoppers who summered there asked why the service was available in the Hamptons but not the Shore. She said she received a barrage of requests from women who said, "Why don't you like the Shore?"

Kaminetsky likes to talk as if she's a personal shopper. When a customer told her she wanted a pair of Khaite's sold-out, half-calf leopard pants, she reached out to her counterpart and the Khaite CEO made it happen. The brand made a single pair just for the customer, Khaite confirms.

Net-a-Porter is introducing a live-map tracking system that lets customers see the location of their parcels, similar to ordering an Uber.

It has reintroduced brands such as Comme des Garçons and added new labels like Willy Chavarria. But it's still missing some prominent names such as Prada and Celine. Kaminetsky said adding more brands is a priority.

The moves have helped Net-a-Porter turn a financial corner. In the quarter that ended June 30, sales increased 4.3%, with the U.S. up more than 13%, compared with a year earlier. Profits grew to 7.4 million euros, or $8.5 million, up from 1 million euros, or $1.2 million the prior year. Top customers spent on average 9.4% more during the quarter than they did during the same period a year ago.

The average order value increased 9% over the past 12 months to 885 euros, or $1,016. That is a key measure for making money in online retailing; it costs roughly the same to ship $100 worth of clothing as it does $1,000. The results include the Mr. Porter men's division.

"This is a company that was struggling and they asked customers what the problems were," said Michael Kliger, LuxExperience's chief executive. "Our customers are highly professional. They are bankers, lawyers and marketing executives. These are smart women. Where else can you find such great advice?"

Stumbles by rivals have thinned the competition. Farfetch narrowly avoided collapsing before it was sold to a South Korean company in 2024. Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus are trying to repair relationships with customers and suppliers after emerging from bankruptcy in June.

Earlier this month, Kaminetsky invited top shopper Sarah Hayden to speak at an employee town hall. The 43-year-old technology executive from London talked about where she thought Net-a-Porter was succeeding and some areas for improvement.

Hayden shared examples of how the personal-shopping service has stepped up. When a bandeau top she had ordered failed to arrive before a recent trip to Spain, her personal shopper had the item rushed to her hotel. Another time, her personal shopper asked Parisian jewelry designer Yvonne Leone to make a ring to fit her finger.

Hayden also said she wished Net-a-Porter had a physical space where she could try on clothes. And she wants to see it carry more brands.

Overall, though, Hayden said in an interview, the company has made big strides.

"I used to shop at a lot of places, but in the last year or so, I shop with Net-a-Porter almost exclusively," she said.

Write to Suzanne Kapner at suzanne.kapner@wsj.com
